# ACC Magnetometer {.unnumbered #acc-magnetometer}

ACC means **antirelaxation coated cell**. The page is designed for weak-RF magnetometry calculations in which wall relaxation can be represented by the entered electron-randomization rate, while optical pumping and spin exchange prepare the atomic state.

## Atom and cell settings {#atom-and-cell-settings}

Alkali A is always active. Alkali B becomes active only when it is a different isotope or element from A. Enter the temperature, nitrogen pressure, electron-randomization rates, mixture density model, and static magnetic field.

The population model is diagonal in the selected quantization basis. For the supported secular RF calculation, choose the static-field direction parallel to the quantization axis. A transverse static field would mix states in a way that the current population model does not retain.

## Pump configuration {#pump-configuration}

Each species has up to three named pumps. A pump specifies:

- D1 or D2 spectral line;
- hyperfine reference transition and relative detuning;
- intensity in µW/cm²;
- propagation direction;
- polarization.

Every active optical frequency is evaluated against every active alkali species. A pump aimed at one species can therefore produce off-resonant pumping of another species, although reported target-specific light shifts follow the selected pump target.

## RF configuration {#rf-configuration}

RF-A drives and reads Alkali A; RF-B is defined conversely. The two species retain self- and cross-spin-exchange coupling even though only one RF source is applied for each displayed response.

Choose the RF axis, sweep bounds, and either a spin observable (F_i) or the cyclic off-diagonal alignment observable (Q_{ij}). The plotted curves are derivatives with respect to RF Rabi frequency or, for optical signals, may be converted to response per nT.

## Probe source modes {#probe-source-modes}

Every pump appears twice in the probe-source selector:

- `PumpN weak` copies the pump spectrum, direction, and polarization but ignores its intensity. It is a non-perturbing detector.
- `PumpN` selects the actual pump as the detected beam. Its configured intensity participates in the spatially uniform [physical-pump feedback model](../theory/uniform-density-matrix-feedback.qmd).
- `Custom` defines an independent weak detector.

The physical-pump solver does **not** scale the configured intensity by the ratio of beam area to cell area.

## Results {#acc-results}

The results are divided into three sections:

1. Ground-state Zeeman properties and populations.
2. Atomic weak-RF response.
3. Optical response of the selected probe source.

The optical panel can display fractional transmission, normalized Stokes parameters, rotation, or ellipticity. It can also display Total, Orientation induced, or Alignment induced responses. For physical-pump readout, the last two are separately closed counterfactual calculations and generally do not add to Total.

See [Interpreting results](interpreting-results.qmd) for the phase convention and line-shape guidance.
